label: rwri
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{rwri} 
Let $0 < a/b < 1$ be a rational number. For all $s \in \mathbb{C}$, we have
\[
M(s, a/b) -  \sum_{q|b} \sum_{l \geq 1} (\log q) q^{-sl} e^{- 2 \pi i a q^{l}/b}
 = -  \sum_{\chi}  A(a, b; \chi) \frac{L'}{L}(s, \chi),
\]
where the sum $\sum_{q|b}$ runs through all the prime divisors of $b$,
$L(s, \chi)$ is the Dirichlet $L$-function with a character $\chi$ modulo $b$, and 
\[
A(a, b; \chi) \equiv
\frac{\sum_{1 \leq x \leq b} \overline{\chi}(x) e^{- 2\pi i a x / b}   }{\phi(b)}.
\]

title: Remark
body_md:
Theorem \ref{claim} is in effect whenever the negation of the Riemann hypothesis is assumed. 
This is because the coefficient $\sum_{\chi}A(a, b; \chi)$  contains terms associated with the principal character
$\chi_{0}$.
Note that $L(s, \chi_{0}) = \zeta(s) \prod_{p|b}(1 - p^{-s})$ for modulo $b$.
